verdict.rationale: Vendor docs cover only a thin slice of lost-key handling: you can remove a lost key from your account, and resetting a Bluetooth key keeps its registration. The backup-key strategy appears only secondhand, in a community comment about Google's guidance to keep one key stored safely and another in daily use, plus a note that kits ship with two keys. Missing for 10: first-party documentation on registering a backup key, explicit statement of what is and is not recoverable after loss (e.g. fallback 2SV methods, resident passkeys on the lost key), account-recovery path when all keys are lost, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the vendor documents a credible lockout-recovery strategy — registering a backup key, and what is and is not recoverable if a key is lost

citations.quote: If you lose your key or decide you don’t want to use it anymore, you can remove it from your account.
Your key will still be registered to your account after it’s reset.
even Google's own guidelines tell you to store one in a safe place and keep the other one in daily use
